metadata.title: Nvidia-Backed Marvell, Lumentum Could Be Nearing a Deal

content.text:
KEY TAKEAWAYS
-
Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, with an announcement possible next week, according to reports.
-
A deal would give Marvell more direct access to a major laser supplier.
Chip designer Marvell Technology and optical components maker Lumentum could be moving toward a merger.
Shares of Marvell Technology (MRVL) were down more than 14% in recent trading, while Lumentum (LITE) climbed a bit less than 1%, after Bloomberg said Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum. An announcement could come as soon as next week, according to the report. Lumentum and Marvell did not respond to Investopedia's requests for comment in time for publication.
A deal would give Marvell, which buys lasers from Lumentum, more direct access to a major supplier. It would also bring together two AI investor favorites, as strong demand has sent both companies' sales and stocks soaring this year.
Lumentum had a market capitalization of about $82.8 billion as of yesterday's close, while Marvell's is just over $220 billion. Shares of both companies were also boosted by a pair of $2 billion investments from Nvidia (NVDA) earlier this year; Marvell in particular got some highly public backing from Jensen Huang.
Marvell recently hiked its long-term sales targets on booming data center demand. Earlier this month, Lumentum's CEO said the company is sold out of its production capacity through early 2029 for its optical networking products.
Marvell shares were up roughly 200% for the year through Wednesday's close, while Lumentum shares have surged 150%.
